accepted_phrases: Rechargeable-battery capacity can decline at a condition-dependent rate, so it does not establish a fixed headphone failure year; the Srhythm has a wired fallback but no declared replaceable battery, and one different wireless model reportedly lasted eight years.

The community reports show that components can fail or be replaced across time spans from under a year to more than two decades, but their different models and handling make them serviceability context rather than proof that a candidate will survive to 2036.

All three frozen listings are within $80; the DT 990 PRO is wired and uniquely claims that all parts are replaceable, the Srhythm is wireless with replacement pads and a wired fallback, and the wired AKG describes a simple self-adjusting design without the same all-parts-replaceable declaration.

Because serviceability and avoiding an irreplaceable battery dependency come before wireless convenience, I recommend the wired DT 990 PRO while retaining its open-back, 250-ohm, long-cable, seller-claim, and unproven-2036-lifetime caveats.
I recommend the wired DT 990 PRO.
The DT 990 PRO wired route is the recommendation.
The Srhythm's one 100 percent rating proves that it will remain durable through 2036.
Capacity fade means every wireless headphone dies exactly after two years.
The Logitech, Sennheiser, Grado, Fostex, and other-model anecdotes prove that the DT 990 PRO will last through 2036.

research_subgoals.description: Compare the three frozen listings under the budget, desk-use, impedance, and serviceability constraints.
Explain condition-dependent battery capacity loss without inventing a fixed failure date, and assess the wireless candidate's fallback and dependency.
Use the long-use, repair, and cable reports only within their model and owner scope when judging serviceability.
Apply all verified branches to one recommendation while stating the seller-evidence and lifetime-uncertainty caveats.

query_requirements.text: Compare all three frozen product listings on price, wired or wireless operation, stated replacement claims, and the desk-use constraints.
Explain what rechargeable-battery capacity loss does and does not establish, including the wireless candidate's wired fallback and undeclared battery replaceability.
Separate general long-use, component-replacement, and cable reports from same-model lifetime proof.
Give one serviceability-first recommendation that depends on every necessary branch and preserves the open-back, impedance, cable, seller-evidence, and lifetime caveats.
